item.text:
**2B.4 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Bottom line:** The evidence is overwhelmingly negative on civilian protection, proportionality, detention, and treatment of the wounded. The only meaningful positive evidence I found is that the ICRC and Ethiopian counterparts ran IHL/IHRL training and that some institutions had at least partial complaint/recommendation machinery. That is mitigation, not proof of compliant operations.

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-09-13 | ICRC Impact in Ethiopia: January - June 2024 Bulletin | International Committee of the Red Cross | [icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024](https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024) | The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL and IHRL for ENDF, police, militias, and other armed groups, explicitly aiming to protect civilians and medical personnel and to improve respect for the laws of war. This is the best positive evidence, but it shows training efforts rather than demonstrated compliance in operations. | 2B.4, 1B.7, 1B.8 |
| 2024-01-12 | Country policy and information note: actors of protection, Ethiopia, February 2024 (accessible) | GOV.UK | [gov.uk/government/publications/ethiopia-country-policy-and-information-notes/country-policy-and-information-note-actors-of-protection-ethiopia-february-2024-accessible](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ethiopia-country-policy-and-information-notes/country-policy-and-information-note-actors-of-protection-ethiopia-february-2024-accessible) | The note says the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission receives complaints and that state/federal institutions implemented some recommendations on human-rights protections and prison conditions. This is weak but relevant positive evidence that some oversight and detention safeguards existed in 2024. | 2B.4, 1B.7 |
| 2024-04-04 | Ethiopia: Military Executes Dozens in Amhara Region | Human Rights Watch | [hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region) | HRW said Ethiopian military forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi on January 29, 2024 and committed other war crimes. This is strong evidence of failure to respect civilian protection, necessity, and proportionality. | 2B.4, 7A.* |
| 2024-03-05 | ‘Horrific’ civilian toll as Ethiopia turns to combat drones to quell local insurgencies | The New Humanitarian | [thenewhumanitarian.org/feature/2024/03/05/horrific-civilian-toll-ethiopia-turns-combat-drones-local-insurgencies](https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/feature/2024/03/05/horrific-civilian-toll-ethiopia-turns-combat-drones-local-insurgencies) | The report describes a February 19, 2024 drone strike on a truck carrying civilians in Amhara that killed at least 30 people. That is direct evidence of likely disproportional or indiscriminate use of force harming civilians. | 2B.4, 7A.* |
| 2024-07-03 | “If the Soldier Dies, It’s on You”: Attacks on Medical Care in Ethiopia’s Amhara Conflict | Human Rights Watch | [hrw.org/report/2024/07/03/if-soldier-dies-its-you/attacks-medical-care-ethiopias-amhara-conflict](https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/07/03/if-soldier-dies-its-you/attacks-medical-care-ethiopias-amhara-conflict) | HRW documented military seizures of ambulances, harassment and arrest of medical staff, raids on hospitals, and at least one apparent drone strike on an ambulance. This is strong evidence of violations affecting the wounded, medical neutrality, and protected transport. | 2B.4, 7A.* |
| 2024-10-08 | Exclusive-UN weighs suspending relief to Ethiopia's Amhara after aid workers attacked, document shows | Reuters | [investing.com/news/world-news/exclusiveun-weighs-suspending-relief-to-ethiopias-amhara-after-aid-workers-attacked-document-shows-3653181](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusiveun-weighs-suspending-relief-to-ethiopias-amhara-after-aid-workers-attacked-document-shows-3653181) | Reuters reported that the UN was considering suspending relief in Amhara after deadly attacks on aid workers, with five aid workers killed in the first half of 2024. This is strong evidence that the conflict environment under Abiy failed to protect humanitarian personnel. | 2B.4, 7A.* |

**Search gap**

- I searched directly for 2024 evidence on civilian protection, humanitarian law, prisoner treatment, necessity, and proportionality.
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence showing Abiy’s military operations were conducted in a way that clearly met IHL standards.
- I also did not find strong public evidence of systematic prisoner-treatment reform in active conflict zones.
- The limited positive evidence is mostly institutional or training-oriented, not battlefield-outcome evidence.

**Assessment**

- Best positive evidence: ICRC IHL/IHRL training and weak institutional complaint/recommendation mechanisms.
- Best negative evidence: Merawi summary executions, combat drone strike on civilians, attacks on medical care, and attacks on aid workers.
- Overall: 2024 conduct looks inconsistent with civilian-protection, proportionality, and protected-treatment norms.
